evidence_basis.originality_note: All seven contexts, values, wording and figure briefs are original. They reproduce assessment demands without copying any official question.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior conservation recall, ratio recognition, interpretation, direct calculation, energy accounting, comparison of matching power ratios, then a mixed kinetic-energy and efficiency ledger

questions.prompt: State the principle of conservation of energy and explain what it implies when some of a machine's input energy is not transferred usefully.
Which expression correctly defines the efficiency of a system?

options.A: total energy input / useful energy output
options.B: useful energy output / total energy input
options.C: non-useful energy output / useful energy output
options.D: useful energy output + total energy input

questions.prompt: A machine has an efficiency of 0.75. Which statement is correct?

options.A: It transfers 0.75% of its input energy usefully.
options.B: It transfers 25% of its input energy usefully.
options.C: It transfers 75% of its input energy usefully.
options.D: Its useful output is 1.75 times its input.

questions.prompt: A blender receives 1.50 kJ and transfers 0.960 kJ usefully to moving food. What is its efficiency?
A polishing machine receives 4.50 kJ of energy. During the same operation, 3.15 kJ is transferred usefully to the rotating pad.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage efficiency of the machine.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the energy transferred in non-useful ways and state an energy-conservation check.

questions.prompt: Two portable solar chargers operate in the same sunlight. Charger P receives 40.0 W and supplies 22.0 W usefully. Charger Q receives 30.0 W and supplies 18.0 W usefully.

figure.purpose: Assess correct identification and comparison of useful output and total input powers.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired comparison diagram. Show charger P with a 40.0 W input arrow and 22.0 W useful output arrow. Show charger Q with a 30.0 W input arrow and 18.0 W useful output arrow. Include an unlabeled loss arrow from each. Do not show formulas, efficiencies or answers.
figure.alt_text: Charger P receives 40.0 watts and supplies 22.0 watts usefully; charger Q receives 30.0 watts and supplies 18.0 watts usefully.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage efficiency of charger P.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage efficiency of charger Q.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State which charger is more efficient and explain why the larger useful power output alone is not enough to decide.

questions.prompt: A ball launcher receives 1.20 kJ of energy. It launches a 0.400 kg ball at 60.0 m s^-1. The kinetic energy of the ball is the useful output of the launcher.

figure.purpose: Assess integration of prior kinetic-energy calculation with a current single-system efficiency ratio and conservation check.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired energy-flow diagram. Show a launcher box with a 1.20 kJ input arrow and a ball leaving, labelled mass 0.400 kg and speed 60.0 m s^-1. Include an unlabeled downward loss arrow. Do not show kinetic energy, efficiency, formulas or answers.
figure.alt_text: A launcher receives 1.20 kilojoules and launches a 0.400 kilogram ball at 60.0 metres per second.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use E_K = 1/2 mv^2 to calculate the useful kinetic energy output of the launcher.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage efficiency of the launcher.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use conservation of energy to calculate the energy transferred in non-useful ways and check the energy ledger.
